newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania Vilnius Bank 9-mo profit rises.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania Vilnius Bank 9-mo profit rises.

text.p: The net income of leading Lithuanian bank Vilnius Bank rose to 16 million litas in the first nine months of the year, up from 11.7 million litas after six months, the bank said on Thursday.
The bank, which has Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) quoted in Luxembourg, said in a statement that its net interest income rose to 32.6 million litas from 17.1 million litas.
Its assets rose to 737.5 million litas from 382.9 million litas at the end of 1995.
"We are a conservative bank and we will remain one," bank chairman Julius Niedvaras told a news conference.
Lithuania was shaken by a banking crisis at the end of last year from which the country is still recovering.
"The bank has increased its share of the deposit market by six percent in the currently complicated situation in the Lithuanian financial markets," the statement added.
It said its total deposits came to 440.42 million litas compared with 243.77 million litas at the end of 1995 and that it now held 12 percent of the deposit market.

It said such a rise in deposits meant there was a mismatch with its loan portfolio which had tried to solve by extending It said its loans rose to 283.83 million litas at the end of nine months, a rise of 68 percent since the start of the year with growth of 57 percent occurring in the third quarter.
The bank said that its loan portfolio was important in its development but did not intend to relax its credit procedures.
